newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends up vs dollar on poor demand.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends up vs dollar on poor demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Friday up against the dollar on lack of demand as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) stayed away from the market, dealers said.
Dealers said the RBI did not buy dollars from the market on Friday but picked up dollars from banks who sold to them.
"They were not in the market but they accepted dollars from banks who went to them," said a dealer.
The rupee ended Friday at 35.840/845 per dollar against its Wednesday close of 35.865/875. Dealers said the rupee traded at a high of 35.84 and a low of 35.87 on Friday.
The forex market was largely inactive on Thursday as banks in India's commercial capital of Bombay were closed for a local holiday.
"Today's movements in the exchange rate are a reflection of the current situation," said one dealer at a foreign bank. "As soon as RBI steps out, the rupee starts moving up."

The rupee fell to 35.89 on Wednesday following sustained dollar purchases by the central bank. Dealers said the RBI bought around $400-500 million from Monday, weakening the rupee from last weekend's close of 35.745/755.
"Basically the problem is one of excess dollar supply and poor demand," said another dealer. "Today even the State Bank of India was selling dollars."
The rupee ended up against the forward dollar also on sale of the US currency by corporates, dealers said.
"Call money has been coming down from Monday's high of 10.5 percent," said a dealer. "Forward premiums also came down as sentiment improved."
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Friday steady at 4.80 percent. It touched of 5.4 percent on Monday.
